issue: Does the 'in interstate commerce' element of a federal statute require proof that an online communication actually crossed state lines, or is it enough to show that the Internet was used?

sides.position: The government can satisfy the 'in interstate commerce' element by showing only that the Internet was used; proof that the communication physically crossed state lines is not required.
cases: United States v. Lewis, 554 F.3d 208 (1st Cir. 2009)
United States v. Harris, 548 F. App'x 679 (2d Cir. 2013)
United States v. MacEwan, 445 F.3d 237 (3d Cir. 2006)
United States v. Runyan, 290 F.3d 223 (5th Cir. 2002)

sides.position: The government must prove that the online communication actually crossed state lines, not merely that it was made over the Internet.
cases: United States v. Wright, 625 F.3d 583 (9th Cir. 2010)
United States v. Schaefer, 501 F.3d 1197 (10th Cir. 2007)

quote: A circuit split has developed around this point.
cite: United States v. Robert Haas, 37 F.4th 1256 (7th Cir. 2022)
